newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run trades up in active start of week.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run trades up in active start of week.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run began the week actively, trading on Monday at slightly higher numbers with the seller saying he sold all his next month's avails as he was bearish on crude.

A 25,000 tonne loader of 0.5 to 0.7 pct sulphur material was sold at $99.75 a tonne fob to a U.S. refiner, who later paid $100.75 for a second similar sized cargo, the last July material held by the seller.
These deals compare with the sale on Friday at a price between $97 and $99 a tonne for a 25 to 30 KT cargo out of Scandinavia into the United States.
"I was more confident, I asked $100.75 (for the second cargo) and got it," the seller said, adding that the buyer has an option to have the cargoes together or separately between July 10 and 25.
"I am bearish on crude, I think it will go down. One doesn't really know what's going to happen in this market so I sold both cargoes," he added.

Other traders said that a Norwegian major was reoffering a cargo it was marketing for an Irish refiner at $97 a tonne, but moved back up to $101 later in the day, when a major buyer disappeared from the market.
"I was offered that cargo at $97 but I am not interested and neither is anyone else," a U.S.-based refiner said of that cargo.
